title: RAG Security & Access Control
interviewAnswer: RAG security requires authorization-aware ingestion and retrieval, not only good prompts. I preserve document permissions as metadata, filter before retrieval, isolate tenants, sanitize untrusted content and test for indirect prompt injection and data exfiltration.
why: RAG can turn a safe LLM into a data-leak system if retrieval ignores who is allowed to see each document.
intuition: The model should never receive a chunk the current user was not authorized to retrieve in the first place.
deepDive: Index-time metadata should retain ownership/ACL information. Query-time filters must be enforced server-side. Source documents should be treated as untrusted content; generated answers should preserve citations/provenance for review.
workedExample: A finance employee asks about HR salaries. Even if the semantic search finds salary documents, ACL filtering must remove them before ranking/context construction.
commonMistakes: Relying on “do not reveal secrets” prompts after unauthorized retrieval.
Sharing one vector namespace across tenants without enforced metadata filters.
followUps: Where should authorization happen in RAG?
production: Add security regression tests with adversarial documents and cross-tenant queries; audit retrieval events separately from LLM generations.
